description: Solo participant focusing on Machine Learning and Data Science for exoplanet detection and space data analysis with zero data leakage methodology.
summary:
SPHEREx Sky Time-Lapse: see the sky move.
The problem. SPHEREx maps the whole sky every six months in 102 infrared bands, producing far more images than anyone can inspect by hand. Moving objects like comets, asteroids and brown dwarfs reveal themselves only by shifting position between images.
Our solution. A web tool where you pick a patch of sky and watch real SPHEREx images play like a short video, so movers stand out to the eye.
What it does
Plays a time series of real SPHEREx cutouts, with adjustable speed and contrast.
Filters by wavelength window and by detector array (D1–D6), so you compare like with like. SPHEREx sees the same spot at different wavelengths on different dates, so this step is essential.
Stacks frames to cut noise, subtracts the window mean, and lets you add or subtract any two frames you choose (A − B, A + B) to expose changes in position or brightness.
Tap any pixel to get its spectrum on the fly, and export it as CSV.
Shows per-frame metadata and quality-flag fractions, so users know how reliable each image is.
Overlays Gaia DR3 (moved to each frame's date using proper motion) and AllWISE sources, switchable on and off.
Lets users enter RA/Dec and change the field of view.
New data loads from a simple JSON file, so the tool is easy to update as SPHEREx releases more.
